gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-khudawadi: Irish Grover stands tall and sturdy, with a faint thick-and-thin rhythm that keeps it playful. And Noto Sans Khudawadi is the plain sans that does the quiet work, its rounds left unlatched while the heading carries the personality.
gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-kr: Big, sturdy lowercase with softly varied strokes gives Irish Grover its homespun, slightly goofy charm. But Noto Sans KR is the steadier half, with generous curve gaps and a large x-height that let it hold the plain, clear voice.
gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-lao: Chunky, friendly and a bit wobbly. Irish Grover keeps its thin strokes sturdy while Noto Sans Lao, a plain sans with a lifted x-height and open mouths, carries long paragraphs with a smooth, uncramped flow.
gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-lao-looped: Noto Sans Lao Looped reads in solid blocks of text rather than jagged skylines, with bowls left unfinished on one side. Irish Grover, by contrast, brings a gentle thick-to-thin wobble, so the two feel like a handshake between playful and practical.
gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-lepcha: Noto Sans Lepcha has wide-open curves and lowercase with the stature of cast iron capitals, which makes it the workhorse here. Yet Irish Grover does the showing off best, its lightly modulated strokes feeling hand-shaped and cheerful.
gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-limbu: Noto Sans Limbu has gaping curves and tall-bodied small letters, giving it a frank, open look. Noto Sans Limbu over a long page feels easy and unhurried, while Irish Grover above it adds a mild, soft-edged swagger.
gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-lisu: Noto Sans Lisu tucks its ascender tops close to the x-height line and opens its s curves wide, giving a tidy, level texture. Over many lines it keeps moving smoothly.
gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-lydian: Irish Grover's tall, sturdy lowercase makes every word look big and slightly bouncy. Noto Sans Lydian then settles the page, its capitals barely taller than lowercase, so a long read feels low-key and approachable.
gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-mahajani: Chunky, bouncy, hard to ignore. Irish Grover handles the loud part, and Noto Sans Mahajani, a plain sans with funnel-wide e shapes and tall lowercase, reads steadily and cleanly for as long as you care to go.
gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-malayalam: Sturdy letters with a soft, hand-made wobble. Irish Grover is best at bringing gentle thickening and thinning to a headline, but Noto Sans Malayalam, a plain sans, is best at keeping its middle zone full and its s generous.
